subject: Am I using the 'fit' argument of the 'stan' function correctly?

messages.author: 885539f3f5ae8fd5
messages.subject: Am I using the 'fit' argument of the 'stan' function correctly?
parts:
Hi,

I just wanted to check that I'm using the 'fit' argument of the 'stan' function (in Rstan) correctly. I am running a Monte Carlo simulation where some of my conditions that vary (such as number of items) affect how the model code is written and others (such as sample size) do not. This is probably due to my lack of familiarity of how to write good stan code, but that's the way it is right now. Do I need to compile one model fit object for every combination of conditions that vary (here, every combination of item length and sample size) regardless of whether they affect the stan model code, or can I save extra time by compiling one model fit object just for every combination of conditions that affect how the model code is written (here, every item length) and use that same fit object for different sample sizes with the same item length?

Thanks for the help,
Jon

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Am I using the 'fit' argument of the 'stan' function correctly?
parts:
If you write the Stan program to input things like n_length to the data block, then it should be fine. When stan() is passed a fit argument, it will pass whatever is in its data argument --- which can be different from when stan() was called originally --- to a new instance of the C++ object that does the sampling.

Ben
